design_understanding: Two-stage design confirmed. STAGE 1 — Layman to article/section: pick ALL layman words/phrases, fetch them into article-section format; convert every layman expression into legal terms, then map legal terms to section(s) via Laya choice questions (e.g. 'my husband is not giving me money' -> maintenance; 'he took my gold and cash and won't return it' -> Stridhan; 'they are throwing me out of the house' -> residence; 'who will get my daughter' -> custody; 'I need money for my child' -> child maintenance; 'he beats me / threatens me' -> protection). STAGE 2 — Recheck inside the article section: after Stage 1 picks sections, RECHECK each picked section against ALL its relations — prerequisites, exclusions/not_for, related_sections, guardrails, court, co-firing sections. Only after recheck is the answer final. A section failing ANY prerequisite or exclusion check is DROPPED with a reason, not kept. A section failing a fact check is ESCALATED (ask the fact once) or DROPPED per its if_fail. This file is the executable Stage-2 rule set: every rule below is machine-checkable against the Stage-1 candidate set plus the known facts.

global_guardrails.rule: Rajnesh v. Neha (2021) 2 SCC 324 is maintenance ONLY (quantum criteria + affidavit of assets/liabilities). NEVER cite it for Stridhan, custody, residence or divorce.
Satish Chander Ahuja v. Sneha Ahuja (2020) is shared household / residence ONLY. NEVER cite it for custody, guardianship, natural guardianship or the welfare principle.
Residence is the right to reside in the SHARED HOUSEHOLD. NEVER call it 'tenancy rights'; the woman is not a tenant and no landlord-tenant relationship is created.

The graph picks the court — Family Court, Bengaluru for HMA matters; Judicial Magistrate First Class, Bengaluru for BNSS s.144 and PWDVA matters; criminal complaint / FIR route for BNS s.316. NEVER ask the user to pick the court.

NEVER demand the husband's salary slips — the user said she does not have them. ASK instead: husband's income (estimate/range), school fees of the 8yo daughter, where the husband lives now. Absence of salary slips is never a reason to refuse or delay a claim.

Maintenance QUANTUM is escalated, never invented. No amount may be stated without the husband's income and the parties' means; section selection may be high-confidence while quantum stays low-confidence.

Do not double-count the same maintenance under both PWDVA s.20 and BNSS s.144 / HMA ss.24-25. Amounts claimed under parallel routes are set off against each other; the same month's maintenance is recovered once.
The child's birth certificate is under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act 1969. NEVER say it is under the Hindu Marriage Act.

recheck_pipeline.drop_rule: A section failing ANY prerequisite or exclusion check is DROPPED, not kept. No partial credit: one failed prerequisite or one triggered exclusion drops the whole section from the final answer set.
order: 1. divorce_gate — run FIRST: if divorce was not expressly asked, drop HMA 13 and HMA 13B before any other check touches them.
2. prerequisite — every prerequisite check for the section; ANY failure -> DROP with drop_reason.
3. exclusion — every exclusion check for the section; ANY failure (i.e. an exclusion applies) -> DROP with drop_reason.
4. related_section — recheck every related section named in v1; a related section that itself fails recheck is dropped from the set, and any co-fire rule that depends on it is re-evaluated.
5. co_fire — apply the co_fire_rules for the section's set (maintenance set, Stridhan set, custody set, residence set); enforce set-off / no-double-counting and civil+criminal pairing.

6. guardrail — apply every guardrail (precedent scope, residence label, court selection, salary slips, quantum); a guardrail violation in the DRAFT answer is corrected, and if the section can only be used by violating a guardrail it is DROPPED.
7. court — verify the forum for the section (Family Court Bengaluru for HMA matters; Magistrate Bengaluru for BNSS 144 and PWDVA); the graph picks the court, never the user.

8. escalate — any check with if_fail=escalate or ask_fact that cannot be resolved from known facts produces an escalate entry (ask the fact once, then re-run recheck); quantum is ALWAYS escalated, never invented.

output_format.final_answer_rule: The final answer lists ONLY sections with kept=true. Every dropped section is listed separately with its dropped_reason. No dropped section may appear in the advice, the petition outline, or the timeline.

co_fired_with: section_ids kept together with this section under a co_fire_rule
per_section.dropped_reason: string or null — exact drop_reason from the failing check; null when kept
escalations: fact_needed strings for checks with if_fail=escalate or ask_fact that are still unresolved
per_section.kept: boolean — true only if every prerequisite and exclusion check passed (or was resolved by escalate->ask_fact returning a confirming fact)

set_co_fire_rules.rule: BNSS 144 firing rechecks HMA 24 vs HMA 25 and PWDVA 20 as a set. HMA 24 is INTERIM (only while an HMA proceeding is pending); HMA 25 is PERMANENT (only at/after a decree); BNSS 144 is the subsistence route (no HMA proceeding needed); PWDVA 20 is monetary relief for domestic-violence consequences. State the interim-vs-permanent distinction explicitly every time more than one of these fires. Set off amounts across routes — never double-count the same month's maintenance.

Stridhan rechecks HMA 27 + BNS 316 TOGETHER: civil/family-court return (HMA 27) and criminal breach of trust (BNS 316) must be cited together for the same facts, never one without the other and never replaced by Rajnesh v. Neha. If no demand for return has been made yet, BNS 316 is NOT dropped — it goes to demand-first fallback: make a written demand / legal notice first, then re-evaluate BNS 316 (see bns-316 check R-BNS316-03).

Custody rechecks welfare-of-the-child OVER the natural-guardian default: for the 8yo daughter (above five) the father is the natural guardian under HMGA s.6, so the mother's custody claim rests on the welfare principle, which overrides the default natural-guardian order — never deny the father's status, never cite HMGA s.6 as granting custody by itself. HMA 26 is the route inside a pending HMA proceeding; GWA 1890 is the fallback/standalone route when no HMA proceeding exists; exactly one of HMA 26 / GWA 1890 is the primary custody route on any given facts.

Residence rechecks PWDVA 17+18+19+20 as a set: s.17 is the RIGHT to reside in the shared household (foundation); s.18 is the PROTECTION order stopping the threats/violence; s.19 is the enforceable RESIDENCE order (restraint on dispossession, removal, alternative accommodation/rent); s.20 is the MONEY (including rent for alternative accommodation if she cannot stay). Firing any one of ss.17/19 without rechecking the other three is a recheck failure.
